scenes.sub: Know exactly what to do when a protocol you use is exploited, a stablecoin depegs, or your wallet is compromised.

scenes.title: Explanation — the 60-minute playbook
scenes.vo: 0–5 min: Verify. Official channels only (bookmarked X/Discord/status page, security firms). Don't click links in DMs, and don't sign anything "to protect funds". 5–20 min: Contain. 20–60 min: Stabilise. Check HFs across all positions (prices may be moving), top up from the reserve, and journal every action with timestamps. After: Review. What was the signal, what worked, and what changes in the caps and the register? Protocol exploit: withdraw if still possible and safe; revoke approvals to affected contracts. Depeg: follow your written peg rule (for example exit below 0.99 for X hours); don't panic-sell far below it on a thin book. Wallet compromise: move remaining assets to a fresh wallet (new seed, clean device); revoke approvals; assume the old seed is burned.
scenes.cap: Protocol exploit: withdraw if still possible and safe; revoke approvals to affected contracts. lines: Someone offers a link to "rescue your funds". What do you do?
scenes.sub: Answer: Ignore it. It's a common scam during incidents.

lines: Wallet compromised: can you keep using the seed?
scenes.sub: Answer: No. Move to a fresh wallet with a new seed; the old one is burned.
